To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relaxin family peptides are potent and specific activators of the G protein-coupled receptors LGR7 and 8.

RLF and LRF, two members of the relaxin family of peptides, act through two members of a novel family of G-protein-couple receptors to control testicular descent and ovarian folliculogenesis in mammals, respectively.
relaxin and its receptor LGR7, and RLF and its receptor LRG8, are structurally and functionaly similar and that the receptors have similar signal initiation processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and regulation of the relaxin family peptides, their receptors, and their roles in reproductive and non-reproductive tissues and organs.
the discovery, characterization, and physiological function of a new hormone and its receptor.
the structure, expression and function of relaxin and relaxin-like factor, their receptors, and other G-protein coupled receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relaxin/RLF system, in its present state of knowledge, has provided the basis for an important new field of investigation, the G-protein-couple receptor system.
the relaxin family peptides, relaxin and RFL, and their receptors, LGR7 and 8, are the most important and exciting discoveries in the history of reproductive biology.

relaxin is a peptide hormone that is synthesized by the corpus luteum and the myometrium, and by the prostate and seminal vesicle, and that it acts on the uterus and the prostate, and possibly other organs and tissues, by binding to its cognate receptor, LGR7, and initiating a signaling cascade that leads to a variety of physiological effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
relaxin, the relaxins, RLF and the receptors have provided the opportunity for us to learn about the biology of a new class of receptors.
the relaxin family peptides and their receptors have provided a new paradigm of receptor-ligand interaction that has been useful in the study of other receptor systems.
the relaxin/insulin-like factor receptor system is a very important and interesting system to investigate the mechanisms of G-protein activation and signal initiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

relaxin and relaxin-related peptides and their receptors have been identified in a wide variety of species, including humans, and that they have important roles in reproduction, development and tissue remodeling.
the LGR7/LGR8 system is a good example of the complexity of the receptor/ligand interactions in the G-protein-couple receptor system.

RLF and LRG8 have provided a new and useful tool for the study of testicular descent and that relaxin, LGR7 and RLF and LCR8 have provided a useful model for the study of G-protein coupled receptor signaling.
